fixes.new:
A space transport ship operated by the Takeo General Company.
As with the old $$シャトル$$, every employee except $$ワッ太$$ boards it, dividing up duties from piloting to weapons control.
The old $$シャトル$$ was moderately damaged in battle with Jackal, an executive of the Robot Empire, but was rebuilt with funding from the Director-General of the Space Defense Agency, gaining upgrades across the board in firepower, cruising speed, and more.
Its role remains unchanged: it combines with Trider's cruising form, Cosmic, to become the Fortress, and its main uses are transporting supplies and personnel. But thanks to reinforcements better suited for combat, it has become an even more reliable support machine for Trider.
For the managing director, too, the results of the refit -- improved work efficiency without denting the company's own pocket -- seem to have been thoroughly satisfying.
Though its exterior changed dramatically, the interior remains much as it was before. The dining salon is still in place, and the homely atmosphere of the workplace, with employees gathering around the table together, has not changed either.
fixes.reason: mistranslation: 中破 means moderately damaged (between 小破 and 大破), not heavily damaged

fixes.new:
A robot that appeared in Episode 50, 'Prince $$グーラ$$ Dies!'
The seventh $$スペースロボ$$, piloted by $$グーラ$$ after he resolved on a final battle with $$正太郎$$, with the appearance of a Western knight.
$$グーラ$$'s specialty, the sword attack, is powerful, and it also uses tricks such as hurling boulders with an electromagnetic net released from its fingertips. It fought a fierce battle against $$鉄人$$ on the surface of the Moon.
In the end, its sword was seized by $$鉄人$$ and it was cut in two by its own weapon.
fixes.reason: omitted subject: the Japanese 用いる has the robot (Space Robo No. 7) as subject but the English was a subjectless passive and the entry settles who; also 'its fingertips' (指先)

fixes.new:
A giant saucer used by the Space Demon King's forces.
It can carry numerous small saucers as well as Space Robos inside it.
It has been commanded not only by the Majin generals who serve the Space Demon King, but also, on occasion, by Branch, who was lent it by the Demon King and boarded it to lead an attack.
fixes.reason: mistranslation: 魔人将軍 is a class (the Majin generals under the Space Demon King), not one person 'General Majin'; and 'to direct an attack' was wrongly attached to the lending: Branch boarded it and took command of an attack (乗り込み、攻撃の指揮を執った); dropped the added 'himself'

fixes.new:
A super robot that could be called Earth's guardian deity.
When $$タケル$$'s $$ガイヤー$$ falls into danger, the $$ゴッドマーズ$$ emblem appears on the screen inside the cockpit. Taking this as the signal that combination is possible, $$タケル$$ begins the sequence with a cry of '$$ゴッドマーズ$$!' Five robots fly in from different locations around the world -- the Sphinx, which houses $$ガイヤー$$, from Egypt; Uranus, which becomes the right arm, from the Arctic; Titan, which becomes the left arm, from the Indian Ocean; Shin, which becomes the right leg, from Angkor Wat; and Ra, which becomes the left leg, from Easter Island -- and combine with $$ガイヤー$$ in the Six God Combination to form $$ゴッドマーズ$$, a body of super-alloy Positronium powered by anti-proton energy.
Its weapons are not especially numerous: God Fire, fired from the 'G' mark on its abdomen, and Mars Flash, a great sword given physical form from the same 'M' mark. However, since their power scales with $$タケル$$'s psychic abilities, they are more than sufficient in combat. The flip side is that they are also at the mercy of $$タケル$$'s mental state, and there were times when prolonged fighting and exhaustion sapped their power and led to a hard-fought battle.
Even after combining, each of the component robots can separate again, and scenes of them attacking with their own individual weapons, fired from their chests, or in hand-to-hand combat have also been seen.
Its finishing move is 'Final $$ゴッドマーズ$$,' which cleaves the enemy in two by combining Mars Flash with God Fire.
In the final battle against the revived $$ズール$$, it received the prayers of many people and shone gold, unleashing supernatural power.
fixes.reason: omission: 胸から放たれる固有武器 - the individual weapons are fired from the chest; the English dropped 'from the chest'

fixes.new:
A combat mecha that appeared in Episode 57, 'Are You the $$バラの騎士$$...?!'
Piloted by the $$ゲシュタルト$$ members $$スナッパー$$ and $$ナッカー$$, it emerged from among the asteroids approaching Earth and attacked the $$クラッシャー隊$$.
It jammed the summoning of the five god robots with a brainwave-blocking beam fired from its head, cornering $$ガイヤー$$ as it was left unable to combine into $$ゴッドマーズ$$.
However, it was struck in the head by the sudden attack of the $$バラの騎士$$, cutting off the brainwave-blocking beam. Once it allowed the combination into $$ゴッドマーズ$$, it was destroyed in an instant.
fixes.reason: wrong referent: 'attacked the Crusher Team, piloted by the Gestalt members' reads as the Crusher Team being piloted; the Japanese says the Gestalt members Snapper and Nakker piloted the mecha (ゲシュタルトのスナッパーとナッカーの操縦で)

fixes.new:
An AT assembled in Gomor, the capital of the planet Quent.
The 'DT' in its name stands for 'Desert-Trip.'
It carries unique, high-performance equipment, including a Quent-element metal detection sensor with extremely high enemy-detection ability, a pile bunker mounted on its left arm, and a dedicated assault rifle.
Like other Berserga units, it has been customized to suit the battlefield it is deployed to, and this particular unit has been fitted with a sand-tripper unit for desert warfare.
This machine is a restoration of an old unit that had been sitting in a storage center -- 'a wreck, but a quality one,' in the words of $$ゴウト$$, who handled the refit.
It is originally a machine used only by mercenaries from Quent, but with $$シャッコ$$ injured, $$フィアナ$$ boarded it instead and pursued $$キリコ$$, who had become Wiseman's successor.
fixes.reason: mistranslation: 索敵能力 is enemy-detection (searching) ability, not 'target-tracking'

fixes.new:
A ground battleship developed by the Balarant Army.
A type that emphasizes its function as a mothership over gun firepower, it functions largely as a mobile base.
In the early days of the Hundred Years War it achieved results on the ground that could be called invincible, but it eventually faded from use due to its high construction costs and the changes in tactics brought about by the rise of ATs.
Niiba, burning with obsession to bring down $$キリコ$$, wired the control system directly into their own brain just as with the $$エクルビス$$, operating the massive vessel as an extension of their own body.
fixes.reason: pronoun: 'his' for Niiba, whose gender is settled neither by the Japanese (自らの脳 / 自分の肉体) nor by the glossary (no character entry); replaced with neutral 'their'

fixes.new:
The machine completed when Kei's beloved Bronco II, badly damaged, was repaired and, in the process, reinforced and modified using Emaan technology.
The legs of the Bronco II were kept as they were, but at Kei's request -- having taken a liking to the handling when he piloted the Molabar -- that machine's arm units were fitted on. Furthermore, in addition to the sympathetic system, three inertial control systems, two anti-gravity levitation units, and a nuclear reactor with output approaching 500,000 horsepower were installed, and despite being a hasty patchwork job, the result surpassed the performance of conventional Drifados. Thanks to this high performance, a mass-production model was later developed as well.
Another major feature is its Variable Geometry ability, allowing it to take four different forms to suit the situation: its humanoid form, the Orguroid, along with Flyer, Gerwalk, and Tank forms.
When it was completed, the members of the $$ファクトリー$$ discussed what to call the new Bronco II, with everyone throwing out their own suggestions, from 'Valhalla' to 'Gammon.' In the end, $$ファクトリー$$ member Jabby settled on '$$オーガス$$,' taken from the name of a war god from the world he originally came from.
Incidentally, 'Nebulado,' one of the names put forward, was the show's working title back in its planning stages.
fixes.reason: wrong referent + mistranslation: その腕部 are the arms of the Molabar (the machine Kei liked to pilot), not the Bronco II whose legs were kept, so 'its arm units' misleads; and フライヤー is 'Flyer', not 'Fighter'
